topic: Do sunflowers really follow the sun?

sunny.name: Sunny
sunny.look: Young sunflower with a small closed green bud and a face on the bud, thin green stem, eager and bouncy.

voice.de: cheerful, excited young voice, native German
voice.en: cheerful, excited young voice, native English

helga.name: Helga
helga.look: Tall mature sunflower with a big open golden flower head and a face in the brown center, the head always faces east, wise and relaxed.

voice.de: relaxed, wise older female voice, native German
voice.en: relaxed, wise older female voice, native English

shots.scene: Sunrise over a sunflower field. Sunny turns its bud eagerly toward the rising sun in the east. Helga stands next to it, her big flower head facing east.
shots.speaker: sunny

line.de: Guten Morgen, Sonne! Ich folge dir heute *den ganzen Tag*!
line.en: Good morning, sun! I'll follow you *all day long*!

shots.scene: Same field. Helga smiles calmly without moving her head, still facing east.
shots.speaker: helga

line.de: Genieß es, solange du jung bist. Ich schaue nur noch nach Osten.
line.en: Enjoy it while you're young. I only face east now.

shots.scene: Sunset. Sunny's bud now points west toward the setting sun. Helga still faces east.
shots.speaker: sunny

line.de: Und nachts drehe ich mich wieder zurück. Warum machst du nicht mit?
line.en: And at night I turn all the way back. Why don't you join in?

shots.scene: Next morning. The first sun rays hit Helga's flower head and a few bees fly toward her.
shots.speaker: helga

line.de: Weil morgens die Bienen kommen. Und die mögen es *warm*.
line.en: Because the bees come in the morning. And they like it *warm*.

shots.scene: Weeks later. Sunny has bloomed into a big open sunflower facing east. It strains to turn toward the sun but cannot move, looking surprised.
shots.speaker: sunny

line.de: Hey... warum kann ich mich *nicht mehr drehen*?

shots.scene: Mika and Dr. Linde stand in the sunflower field. Mika looks up at the tall sunflowers, then at Dr. Linde.
shots.speaker: mika

line.de: Dr. Linde, folgen Sonnenblumen wirklich der Sonne?
line.en: Dr. Linde, do sunflowers really follow the sun?

shots.scene: Dr. Linde points at a young sunflower's stem while explaining.
shots.speaker: linde

line.de: Nur junge. Tagsüber wächst die Ostseite des Stängels schneller, nachts die Westseite.
line.en: Only young ones. By day the east side of the stem grows faster, at night the west side.

shots.scene: Dr. Linde gestures to a row of blooming sunflowers all facing east, bees buzzing around them in the morning light.
shots.speaker: linde

line.de: Blühende Köpfe schauen nach Osten. So werden sie morgens warm und locken *mehr Bienen* an.
line.en: Blooming heads face east. They warm up in the morning and attract *more bees*.

de.title: Folgen Sonnenblumen wirklich der Sonne? 🌻
de.description: Nur junge Sonnenblumen drehen sich mit der Sonne. Warum blühende Köpfe nach Osten schauen und was die Bienen damit zu tun haben, erklärt Dr. Linde. Mehr Blütengeheimnisse auf @BlütenGeheimnis.

en.title: Do Sunflowers Really Follow the Sun? 🌻
en.description: Only young sunflowers track the sun. Dr. Linde explains why blooming heads face east and what bees have to do with it.
